# Self-study {.unnumbered}

Self-study teaches the concepts of machine learning in six themes. Each theme is a short series of activities: notebooks that you run and complete, and pages that you read or try out in your browser. The notebooks use small public datasets, such as the Palmer penguins and California housing prices, so that you can focus on one concept at a time.

Work through the activities of a theme in order. The [course route](../start-here.qmd#the-course-route) shows when to study each theme.

## At a glance

::: {.ml-glance}

| | You learn |
|------|------------------------------|
| [Theme 1](theme-1.qmd) | What machine learning is, and how to train classification, regression and clustering models with scikit-learn |
| [Theme 2](theme-2.qmd) | The stages of a machine-learning project, and how to prepare, explore, model and evaluate data |
| [Theme 3](theme-3.qmd) | How linear regression, logistic regression and clustering work, and how to choose their settings |
| [Theme 4](theme-4.qmd) | Pipelines and the ColumnTransformer: preprocessing and model in one object |
| [Theme 5](theme-5.qmd) | Decision trees, random forests and gradient boosting |
| [Theme 6](theme-6.qmd) | How to communicate technical work, read machine-learning research and test its ideas |

:::

## Themes

### [Theme 1: Foundations of Machine Learning](theme-1.qmd)

What it means for a program to learn from data, and your first classification, regression and clustering models with scikit-learn.

### [Theme 2: The End-to-End ML Workflow](theme-2.qmd)

One small project from start to finish, then data preparation, data understanding, modeling and evaluation in depth.

### [Theme 3: Supervised & Unsupervised Learning](theme-3.qmd)

A look inside three models: linear regression, logistic regression and K-Means. You train each one with scikit-learn, then build its algorithm yourself.

### [Theme 4: Advanced Scikit-Learn](theme-4.qmd)

Pipelines and the ColumnTransformer, which combine preprocessing and a model in one object that you can cross-validate and tune.

### [Theme 5: Tree-Based Algorithms](theme-5.qmd)

Decision trees, and the two ways to combine many of them: random forests and gradient boosting.

### [Theme 6: Applied ML Research](theme-6.qmd)

Presenting and writing about technical work, reading machine-learning research, and testing an idea from a paper yourself.
